reason: Mechanically confirmed: the configured name is read only in NpcManager.spawnNpc (NpcManager.java:102-105 via resolveNpcName at 338-346), and ShopManager.reload() (ShopManager.java:55-65) swaps the config and closes ShopGUIs but never calls any NpcManager method; NpcManager has no reload/rename entry point at all (only spawnNpc/despawnNpc/respawnFromConfig/cleanupOrphans, NpcManager.java:70-330), and respawnFromConfig is invoked only from onEnable (HilltopVillagePlugin.java:158) and spawnNpc from /hilltop deploy setshop (HilltopCommandHandler.java:1189) and the setup wizard (SetupWizard.java:1031, 1320). So after /hilltop shop reload the live Villager keeps the name resolved at its last spawn, while the command reports success from getShopConfig().getItems().size() (HilltopCommandHandler.java:578-580), and the README/docs tell admins every shop.yml field takes effect after that command (README.md:139, docs/guides/shop-customization.md:38,69 mention npc.name then 'no restart needed'). Two parts of the finding are overstated: the stale name is not permanent (a restart, /hilltop deploy setshop, or the wizard re-runs spawnNpc and renames), and the omission is not an oversight-free path but is consistent with the deliberate 'reload does not rebuild the NPC' contract asserted by ShopManager.java:29 and ShopManagerTest.java:381-387/NpcManagerTest.java:786-795, since applying a new name through spawnNpc would despawn and respawn the entity (and be blocked by the cross-world in-match guard, NpcManager.java:74-84). Net effect is a documented-but-unimplemented partial reload with a one-command workaround and no data loss, so low rather than medium.
